channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Open Machine CEO on Anthropic, OpenAI IPO Potential
item.description: Allie Miller, CEO of Open Machine, shared insights on how top technology companies are managing their AI investments to balance cost and return. She explained that frontier companies typically divide their AI efforts into two groups: one focused on raising the baseline capabilities across departments like finance, legal, marketing, and sales with modest subscription-level spending, and a second, smaller 'frontier' team that operates with significantly higher budgets and greater experimentation freedom. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bonds Fall on Doubts Over Treasury's Plan | Real Yield 8/20/2026
item.description: "Bloomberg Real Yield" highlights the market-moving news you need to know. Today's guests: Ian Lyngen, Head of US Rates Strategy at BMO Capital Markets, Stephanie Roth, Chief Economist at Wolfe Research, Meghan Robson, Head of US Credit Strategy at BNP Paribas, and Milwood Hobbs, Deputy CIO of Oaktree's Strategic Credit Platform. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Agility Robotics CEO on Plans To Go Public, China Rivals
item.description: Peggy Johnson, CEO of Agility Robotics, discussed the company's upcoming public debut, positioning it as the only pure-play US public company focused on humanoid robots with proven commercial applications. Agility Robotics is valued at a $2.5 billion pre-money valuation and expects to go public in the fall. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ChatGPT Can Now Control iMessage, Potentially Raising Apple Privacy Concerns
item.description: OpenAI rolled out support on Thursday for controlling Apple Inc.’s iMessage service via ChatGPT, a move with the potential to raise privacy concerns for the iPhone maker.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: OpenAI, Meta Seek Help to Combat Data Center PR Problem
item.description: Tech firms are trying to quell growing opposition to their AI plans
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: China Says Trump Economic Warfare Won't Solve Iran Crisis
item.description: Anna Ashton, former Defense Department analyst for China, says that the US has significantly weakened its relationships and its weapons stockpiles ahead of President Xi's visit to the US in September and that Xi Jinping feels as if he has the upper hand heading into those talks. Ashton also weighed in on the US positioning in the region amid war with Iran, saying that the US is giving Beijing numerous signals that it's 'abandoning the Pacific as an area of primary focus.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: America’s Battle Over Data Centers: Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg journalists answer your questions about how the demand for AI data centers has sparked outrage across the US in a Live Q&A on Wednesday, Aug. 26 at 1 p.m. EDT.
item.dc:creator: Edward Ludlow, Brody Ford, Emily Birnbaum and Matthew Griffin

item.title: Alibaba's AI Spending Spree, Concerns of Circular AI Financing | Bloomberg Tech 8/20/2026
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down the plunge in Alibaba's profit after the company increased its quarterly capex to almost $10 billion for AI. Plus, a look at how Meta has quietly become one of Microsoft's largest AI customers, and at defense tech startup Castelion's plans to boost production of its hypersonic missile systems. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mayfield Bets on AI’s Earliest Founders
item.description: Mayfield has invested more than $3 billion in AI companies, much of it before founders have built a product or even formed a company. Managing Partner Navin Chaddha joins Bloomberg to discuss why he sees AI as a “100x opportunity,” why venture returns still depend on finding a handful of exceptional founders, and why Mayfield is resisting the industry’s push toward ever-larger funds to stay focused on early-stage investing. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Defense Startup Taking a SpaceX Approach to Missiles
item.description: Defense startup Castelion has raised $1 billion at a $13 billion valuation as it races to scale production of its Blackbeard hypersonic weapon system and develop new long-range and defensive capabilities. Co-founder and CFO Andrew Kreitz discusses why manufacturing thousands of weapons at low cost is the company’s central challenge, and how his experience at SpaceX shaped Castelion’s approach. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Is Now One of Microsoft's Largest AI Customers
item.description: Meta has quietly become one of Microsoft's largest AI customers, spending hundreds of millions of dollars a year to access the Azure cloud service - and reviving concerns around circular business dealings in the AI space. Bloomberg's Brody Ford joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tanner Grigoli of Atlantic Records Looks to Summer Camps to Build his Fan Base
item.description: While much of the fan-building process happens online now, one artist took to East Coast summer camps to reach his audience
item.dc:creator: Ashley Carman

item.title: Anthropic Expects to Match or Top SpaceX’s Record IPO Size
item.description: Anthropic PBC expects to match or beat the size of SpaceX’s record-setting initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter, in the latest sign of overwhelming demand from investors looking to profit from the artificial intelligence boom.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz and Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: Anthropic Plans to Change Data Retention Policy for Advanced AI
item.description: Anthropic PBC plans to allow business customers to keep greater control of their data when using its most capable artificial intelligence models, a stark change from an earlier data retention policy intended to mitigate potential cyberattacks.The Claude chatbot maker expects to roll out a new safety system later this year that will still require enterprise customers to retain data for 30 days but with the option to do so on their own cloud computing infrastructure rather than Anthropic’s, accord
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz

item.title: Walmart Warning Hits Retail and Markets | Open Interest 8/20/2026
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Walmart’s earnings disappoint, flashing a warning sign for the broader retail sector, while the 30-year bond rally unravels and markets question whether Scott Bessent can tame rising yields. State Street’s Lori Heinel breaks down what’s driving the bond market, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig lays out the path forward for crypto regulation, and Brown Harris Stevens CEO Bess Freedman warns New York’s housing policies could make an affordability crisis even worse. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple’s AirPods Should Avoid Meta’s Mistakes
item.description: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Dave Lee explains Apple’s plans for AI-enhanced AirPods and smart glasses, and why the company should learn from Meta’s mistakes. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bitcoin Roars Past $70,000 as Yields Sink, Trump Sparks Optimism
item.description: Bitcoin surpassed $70,000 for the first time in over two months, propelled by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s move to push US bond yields lower and a high-stakes meeting President Donald Trump held with crypto industry leaders. Bloomberg's Mike McGlone joins to discuss bitcoin as well as the recent climb in oil. Oil climbed to the highest in almost a month due to Donald Trump’s threat to crush the Iranian economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Robinhood CEO Tenev Talks Crypto Rules and Prediction Markets
item.description: Robinhood co-founder and CEO Vlad Tenev says clearer, more permanent crypto rules would give investors confidence that regulations won't shift with changing administrations. Speaking with Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission in Washington, DC, Tenev says that prediction markets will survive regardless of whether the Supreme Court sides with states seeking to regulate them, though he notes that the industry may have to adapt to the legal outcome. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Super Micro Says Current Leaders Weren’t Aware of Smuggling Plot
item.description: Super Micro Computer Inc. completed an independent probe into the alleged smuggling of Nvidia Corp. chips into China, with the investigation team concluding the company’s current senior management had no knowledge of the purported scheme.
item.dc:creator: Debby Wu

item.title: Muon Space Raises $250 Million in Round Backed by Google
item.description: Satellite startup Muon Space Inc. closed a $250 million funding round, raising capital from Alphabet Inc.’s Google and Salesforce Ventures LLC after launching 11 satellites into orbit and opening a manufacturing facility in California.
item.dc:creator: Yash Roy
